obligation: MTSA report of an actual or threatened cyber incident
trigger: Evidence of an actual or threatened cyber incident involving or endangering the Port plant, including any data, network, program, or system on it
deadline: Immediately
notify: FBI, CISA (for any cyber incident), and the Coast Guard Captain of the Port
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Port plant (MTSA facility). Default for runbook 2: report if any Port plant system is affected or endangered
owner: Facility Security Officer (Port plant) with the CySO

obligation: Reportable cyber incident to the National Response Center (if not reported under 6.16-1)
trigger: Reportable cyber incident (101.615 definition) not already reported to the Coast Guard under 6.16-1
deadline: Without delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Port plant; the company reports under 6.16-1, which satisfies this row
clock_starts: When the incident is identified as reportable

obligation: Breach of security or suspicious activity at an MTSA facility
trigger: Activity that may result in a TSI, or a breach of security (for example an intruder manipulating access control or the dock transfer system)
deadline: Without delay
clock_starts: When the activity or breach is known

trigger: A TSI at the Port plant (for example a cyber-caused release at the dock that disrupts the port)
deadline: Without delay; then follow the FSP
notify: Captain of the Port; then the NRC as the FSP directs

trigger: Release at or above the RQ in 24 hours: ammonia 100 lb; sulfuric acid 1,000 lb; sodium hydroxide 1,000 lb; sodium hypochlorite 100 lb
deadline: Immediately, as soon as the person in charge knows of the release
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - any site, regardless of cause
clock_starts: When the person in charge knows of the release
owner: VP EHS and Process Safety (Shift Supervisor calls 911 first)

trigger: Release of an EPCRA extremely hazardous substance or CERCLA substance at or above its RQ
deadline: Immediately
notify: LEPC community emergency coordinator and the SERC of any state likely to be affected

trigger: After an immediate EPCRA notice
deadline: As soon as practicable after the release

obligation: RMP emergency response and community notification (responding source)
trigger: Accidental release from the Ammonia Unit that may affect the public
deadline: Per the emergency response plan: inform the public and response agencies; activate community notification
notify: Public in the affected area; county fire rescue; LEPC
clock_starts: At the start of the release

trigger: Incident that resulted in, or could reasonably have resulted in, a catastrophic release (a manipulated Ammonia Unit setpoint meets this test)
deadline: Start as promptly as possible, not later than 48 hours after the incident
notify: Internal (Process Safety Manager); report kept 5 years

trigger: Incident that resulted in, or could reasonably have resulted in, a catastrophic release in the workplace (Ammonia or Peroxide Unit)
deadline: Start as promptly as possible, not later than 48 hours

trigger: Accidental release meeting the 68.42 accident history criteria
deadline: Within 6 months of the release, or by the next RMP update if earlier

obligation: RMP public meeting after an accident with offsite impacts
trigger: RMP reportable accident with known offsite impacts
deadline: Within 90 days of the accident

obligation: OSHA severe injury and fatality report
trigger: Work-related fatality; in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye
deadline: Fatality within 8 hours; hospitalization, amputation, or eye loss within 24 hours
clock_starts: At the death or the in-patient admission, amputation, or eye loss

trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents (employee data in HR, payroll, or file shares)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (15-day extension for good cause applies only to this notice)
notify: Affected Florida residents (current and former employees)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - employee data; customer data in TTRS is business contact data and usually not personal information under the statute (counsel confirms)
owner: General Counsel with the HR Director

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (no extension)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if 500 or more Florida residents (about 800 of 850 employees live in Florida)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: More than 1,000 individuals notified at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if current and former employees affected exceed 1,000

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: HR, payroll, or other vendor holding personal information determines a breach
deadline: Within 10 days after determination (vendor duty; contract requires 72 hours)

citation: State breach notification statutes (each state where affected individuals reside)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents of other states (about 6% of employees live in Georgia or Alabama)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply each state's law by residence

citation: TTRS master services agreement, security addendum (contract)
trigger: Security incident affecting TTRS customer data or service availability
deadline: Within 72 hours of confirmation (contract)
notify: TTRS customers' designated contacts (420 tanks, about 300 customer accounts)
owner: Director of Customer Solutions with the General Counsel

trigger: Any suspected security incident that may lead to a claim
deadline: As soon as practicable; call the carrier hotline before hiring incident vendors

trigger: Material incident affecting operations
deadline: Per the agreements (CFO keeps the terms)
notify: Administrative agent; PE sponsor board members

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

trigger: Significant security incident at a covered facility
deadline: Not enforceable (authority lapsed 2023-07-28)
applies_at_this_tier: No - CFATS not reauthorized; the 6.16-1 report reaches CISA anyway

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief; 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - proposed only; as proposed the company would be covered

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a registrant
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination
